title: Cluster Sampling
breadcrumb: Sampling theory → Cluster sampling → One-stage estimators and design effect
engineName: Select groups as primary sampling units and estimate using cluster totals.
objectives: Distinguish elements, clusters and primary sampling units.
Calculate one-stage cluster estimators of totals and means.
State design variance under SRSWOR of clusters.
Interpret ICC, design effect and effective sample size.
Explain operational benefits and precision limitations.

traps: The primary sampling unit is the cluster, not the individual.

howto: Identify the primary sampling unit and whether all elements are observed. For one-stage SRSWOR of clusters, calculate each sampled cluster total, average those totals and multiply by M. For equal cluster size, divide by N=Mm for the element mean. Use the design-effect approximation only after stating its assumptions.

scenes.title: Elements and clusters
body: A cluster is a naturally occurring group of population elements, such as a village, school or household. In cluster sampling, groups are selected first.
In one-stage cluster sampling, every element in a selected cluster is measured. The cluster is the primary sampling unit.
Let M be the number of clusters and t_j the total value in cluster j. Cluster totals are distinct from element values and cluster means.

items.recall: A group of population elements treated as a sampling unit.
refresh: Clusters are existing groups such as villages or schools.
The cluster is selected as the primary sampling unit.
Elements are individual people, farms or records inside it.

items.recall: Select clusters and observe every element in each selected cluster.
refresh: Select a sample of clusters from the frame.
Measure every element in each selected cluster.
Sampling only some elements within selected clusters is two-stage sampling.

items.recall: The sum of element values within a cluster.
refresh: Add all element values in cluster j to obtain t_j.
Cluster totals are the observed values for one-stage cluster estimation.
A cluster total is not an individual value or cluster mean.

ask.q: What is selected randomly in one-stage cluster sampling?
ask.nudge: Clusters are the primary sampling units.

scenes.title: Why sample clusters?
scenes.objective: Explain operational efficiency and precision trade-offs.
body: Listing every individual in a dispersed population can be expensive. A survey can list villages, select some villages and enumerate households in them.
Cluster sampling can reduce travel and setup costs. But people within a cluster may resemble one another, so observations can contain less independent information than an SRS of individuals.
The gain is often logistical rather than statistical. The design effect describes the precision cost of within-cluster similarity.

scenario.title: Fieldwork costs versus information
body: A district contains 80 villages, each with approximately 40 households. Selecting households scattered across all villages may require long travel times and repeated setup costs. Instead, the team selects a smaller number of villages and interviews every household in each selected village. This one-stage cluster design makes fieldwork more concentrated and the village is the primary sampling unit.

Households in one village may share water access, local prices and infrastructure, making their outcomes correlated. The design may be cheaper to operate but less statistically efficient per interview than a well-spread individual sample. Both cost and within-village similarity matter when choosing the design.
scenario.q: What is the main operational advantage?
scenario.answer: It concentrates fieldwork and can reduce listing and travel costs.

ask.q: Why can many interviews in a few villages reduce precision?
ask.nudge: Outcomes within a village may be correlated and partly redundant.

scenes.title: Expand cluster totals
scenes.objective: Calculate an estimated total from sampled clusters.

viz.caption: M=20 and n=4 gives expansion factor M/n=5.

body: With M=20 clusters and four selected clusters having totals 20, 25, 30 and 25, the sample mean cluster total is 25.
Expanding this mean by M gives an estimated population total of 500. The estimator uses cluster totals because whole clusters are observed.
For equal cluster sizes, divide the estimated total by the known number of population elements to estimate the element mean.

ask.q: What is the expansion factor for M=20 and n=4?
ask.nudge: Divide population clusters by sampled clusters.

scenes.title: One-stage cluster estimators
scenes.objective: State total, mean and variance estimators.

blocks.body: There are M clusters with totals t₁,…,t_M. SRSWOR selects n clusters. Let f_c=n/M and S_t² be the finite-population variance among cluster totals.
Ŷ_cl=M t̄_s=M(1/n)Σ_{j∈s}t_j. It is design-unbiased for Y=Σ_jt_j.

blocks.h: Element mean for equal cluster size
blocks.body: If each cluster contains m elements and N=Mm, then Ȳ_cl=Ŷ_cl/N and V(Ȳ_cl)=V(Ŷ_cl)/N².
If cluster sizes differ, an element mean needs a suitable total-over-known-N or ratio construction. The unweighted mean of cluster means is not automatically the element mean.

flow.title: One-stage cluster sampling
flow.alt: List clusters, select a sample, measure every element in selected clusters, calculate cluster totals and expand their mean by M.
flow.note: Variance is based on variation among cluster totals.

steps.say: Calculate the sample mean cluster total.
steps.why: Sampled cluster totals are the observed values.

steps.say: Expand by the population cluster count.
steps.why: The sample mean estimates the population mean cluster total.
There are 20 clusters with five elements each.

scenes.title: Complete the design-effect calculation
scenes.objective: Calculate design effect and effective sample size.
scenes.problem: Average cluster size m=8, ICC ρ=0.25 and 160 interviewed elements. Complete the approximation.

blank.hint: One plus cluster size minus one, times ICC.

steps.why: It accounts for correlation among elements within a cluster.
Seven within-cluster correlations add 1.75 to one.

steps.say: Divide nominal sample size by DEFF.
steps.why: This is the approximate SRS-equivalent sample size.

ask.q: What happens to DEFF as positive ICC increases?
ask.nudge: It increases, reducing effective sample size.

blocks.body: The intraclass correlation coefficient ρ describes similarity between outcomes for two elements in the same cluster.
For approximately equal cluster size m, DEFF≈1+(m−1)ρ. This compares variance with an SRS of the same number of elements.
n_eff≈n/DEFF. A design effect above one means less precision than an SRS with the same nominal element sample size.
This is an approximation. Unequal cluster sizes, unequal weights and complex designs can change the design effect.

ask.q: If ρ=0, what does the approximation give?

scenes.title: Guided practice: estimate a total
scenes.problem: There are M=12 clusters. A sample of n=3 has cluster totals 15, 18 and 21. Estimate the population total.
hints: Keep cluster count separate from element count.
scenes.check: Sample mean is 18 and expansion factor is 12.

scenario.title: Schools as primary sampling units
body: A state education survey lists 300 schools and selects 30 by simple random sampling. In each selected school, the survey measures every enrolled student's attendance days for the reference month. The school total is the sum of attendance days for all students in that school. The design is one-stage cluster sampling because all students in a selected school are included.

The estimated state total is the number of schools multiplied by the sample mean of school totals. If the objective changes to average attendance per student, the analyst must also use the total number of students in the population or an appropriate ratio estimator; simply averaging school means gives each school equal weight, not each student.
scenario.q: What is the primary sampling unit?

solution.say: The sample mean of cluster totals is (15+18+21)/3=18.

ask.q: Why expand school totals rather than student values?
ask.nudge: Schools are the sampled primary units.

scenes.title: Avoid cluster-sampling traps
scenes.objective: Distinguish cluster sampling from other designs.

items.claim: In one-stage sampling, all elements in a selected cluster are observed.
items.why: That is the defining one-stage rule.

items.claim: The primary sampling unit is an individual element.
items.why: The primary sampling unit is the cluster.

items.claim: The total estimator is M times the sample mean cluster total.
items.why: The sample mean cluster total estimates the population mean cluster total.
Within-cluster similarity makes observations partly redundant.
This is the common equal-size approximation.

items.claim: Cluster sampling always gives more precision than SRS of individuals.
items.why: It often trades precision for operational savings.

scenes.title: Transfer: compare effective sample sizes
scenes.objective: Compare design effects for two cluster sizes.
scenes.problem: Two surveys each interview 200 people. A has m=10 and ρ=0.10; B has m=5 and ρ=0.10. Compare design effects and effective sample sizes.
hints: Smaller clusters reduce the penalty when ICC is positive.
scenes.answer: A: DEFF=1.9 and n_eff≈105.26. B: DEFF=1.4 and n_eff≈142.86. B has larger effective sample size.
scenes.check: Both surveys interview 200 people; average cluster size differs.

solution.say: Smaller clusters in B reduce the approximate penalty.

ask.q: At fixed interviews and positive ICC, what is the usual effect of smaller clusters?
ask.nudge: They reduce DEFF and increase effective sample size.

scenes.title: Cluster sampling checklist
scenes.objective: Summarise estimation, variance and design effect.
body: One-stage cluster sampling selects clusters and observes every element in each selected cluster. Cluster totals are the sampled values.
Under SRSWOR of M clusters, estimate the total by Ŷ_cl=M t̄_s, with variance M²(1−n/M)S_t²/n.
For equal cluster size m and known N=Mm, estimate the element mean by Ŷ_cl/N.
For approximately equal cluster size, DEFF≈1+(m−1)ρ and n_eff≈n/DEFF. Positive ICC reduces effective information.
Cluster sampling can lower fieldwork costs but does not guarantee higher precision. Distinguish one-stage cluster sampling from two-stage and stratified sampling.

ask.q: Which estimator and key design condition should you remember for Cluster Sampling?
ask.nudge: State the estimator, its weighting or expansion rule, and the assumptions behind its variance.
